Bind the work tree to a git tree, run Layer 1 on an exported snapshot of it and write one ledger check row (witness: aegis). A label, not proof: only CI on the landing commit confirms it. A tree git cannot see completely (assume-unchanged or skip-worktree files) or that holds symbolic links is unbindable and writes no row; exit 0 only when the run passed

Output format (github, with --ci only: workflow-command annotations)

Post-lane gate: check the lane's commits since merge-base(--base, HEAD) for containment (every changed path, deletions and both sides of a move included, inside the lane's globs) and Python test integrity (removed tests, added skips or xfails, pytest collection changes; assert weakening is not detected). Any finding fails. Self-attested from the live lease or --paths; witnessed with --base-policy. As a CI job it is advisory in v4.1, and a witness is only as strong as the protection on .github/** and on the base branch

Report the cross-lane call, def and import edges between lanes planned with --split (at least two), and the [FROZEN_SIGNATURES] of the functions that cross a lane boundary. Python, and Rust when its driver is enabled. A report: it changes nothing and exits 0 even when it finds edges

Print the day-0 card: languages, AST drivers, rules by type, the Layer 1 pass rate on the files and the 5 files with the most findings (above 2000 files it samples, and says so). Changes nothing and never reads baseline.json; --json for the machine-readable form

Record every current Layer 1 finding in .aegis/baseline.json, so that aegis check then fails only on new ones. Findings are fingerprinted by rule, path, matched line and its occurrence, not by line number. A failure that is not about a line (a rule that cannot load, a file that cannot be parsed) is listed and is never recorded
Drop the entries of .aegis/baseline.json whose findings are fixed (or whose file is gone). It never adds a finding, and it refuses to run while a check cannot run

The CI weakening check: compare the rules that bind (gates, invariants, enforcement: gate) at merge-base(--base, --head) with those at --head, and flag every way one binds less (a deletion or archive, a rank decrease, lost coverage of existing files, a forbid_ast pattern no longer covered, a new or unknown key, any applies_to change, or a mandatory rule added past the scan's slot cap). A flagged change passes only with a signed Aegis-Approve commit (aegis approve) by a key in the base branch's allowed_signers. Also runs T5 fix-commit regression checks (advisory at default warning tier; blocking at gate tier via --strict or user config regression.tier="gate"). Exit 0 pass, 1 fail
With --ci: the commit under review (default: the pull request head in $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, else HEAD)
With --partition: one planned lane and the globs of its files; give at least two. They match as rule target_paths do: a glob without '/' matches at any depth

With --ci: the pull request's base (default: its base.sha in $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, else as below). With --lane: the base branch (default: origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF, $GITHUB_BASE_REF, origin/main, main, origin/develop or develop). A shallow clone fails: fetch with fetch-depth 0. Without --lane: read .aegis/baseline.json from REF (label baseline: base@<sha>; absent there means empty: baseline: absent at base) and check what changed since REF; the working tree's baseline is then not consulted, and a REF that does not resolve is an error. Without --base the working tree's baseline is used and labelled self-attested: a candidate can edit its own. There is no CI detection

With --lane: the lane's globs instead of its live lease (self-attested). They match as rule target_paths do: a glob without '/' matches at any depth, so CHANGELOG.md also admits docs/CHANGELOG.md. They never allow .aegis/** or .github/workflows/**

With --lane: take lanes.<lane> and shared from .aegis/team.json at the base tip, never the candidate; refuses --paths. Only then is the result 'witnessed: base policy', and only then may .aegis/** and .github/workflows/** change
With --ci: run pytest with diff coverage over changed lines

install.description:
Without --host: install the git pre-commit hook (it runs aegis check --hook).

With --host claude-code|codex-cli|antigravity: register `aegis hook run pre-tool --host <h>` as that host's PreToolUse hook, at user scope (default) or, with --scope project, in the repository's host file, which teammates' hosts will execute. The merge keeps everything else in the file, refuses unparseable, symlinked or hard-linked files, and backs the old file up to ~/.aegis/backups/<stamp>/<scope>/. Codex also gets ~/.codex/rules/aegis.rules and runs the hook only after you trust it in /hooks; Antigravity hooks are unavailable on Windows. aegis doctor shows each host's entries and tier; it cannot confirm that a host runs them. Run it from any directory but your home directory, which Aegis never takes as a workspace, even for --scope user (which changes only your user files).

Known gaps:
  - Edits made through shell commands never reach the edit gate on any host.
  - Codex write_stdin into an interactive shell has no PreToolUse payload, and the Codex Bash payload carries no working directory.
  - Antigravity manage_task with send_input types into a background terminal past run_command.
  - Aegis never emits an 'ask' decision (it fails open on Codex and soft-denies in agy headless runs).
  - The hooks fail open on any Aegis error: they are guardrails, not a security boundary.

Show the per-host scan-before-edit rate from the MCP activity log (.aegis/state/activity.jsonl), per session and per host. Edits are the files a session named in aegis_report_outcome 'files' plus the files of commits inside exactly one session's window (first to last event, plus 15 minutes). Limits: an edit time is an upper bound (report or commit time), so the rate can overstate compliance; uncommitted edits that were never reported are not seen; commits in overlapping sessions count as ambiguous, not as misses; a session with no observed edit is unknown, never 0. A host rate is an aggregate over sessions, not a per-attempt verdict. Reads only.
